summary: Pinecrest Peak lookout, Stanislaus NF, Tuolumne County: built 1934, staffed to 1973 per the Forest Service, no longer standing. Trail to the site is about 11 miles round trip.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 ground cabin
facts.status_note: Stanislaus National Forest says it is no longer standing; the register lists removal as unknown. A trail guide says metal bored into the rock still marks the site.

access.note: A trail guide describes a hike on national forest land from Pinecrest to the site; no closure is mentioned in any source read.

visit.trail_note: About 11.2 miles round trip from Pinecrest with about 2,500 feet of climbing. A shorter route starts on Herring Creek Road, about 4 to 5 miles round trip.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest

events.note: Register follows the 1986 Thornton Survey for a 1934 construction date. July 1934 newspaper items describe the station being built and then completed that month.
Stanislaus National Forest note, as quoted by the register: staffed from 1939.

Stanislaus National Forest note: staffed to 1973. The trail guide repeats the 1939-1973 span but also says a small station stood near the peak until about the mid-1970s, a later date that no source read explains.
Registered December 29, 2019, nominated by Brad Eells.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register follows the 1986 Thornton Survey and the July 1934 newspaper items describe a new station that year. The Stanislaus note says it was originally built as a National Defense Observation Tower during World War II. The story uses 1934 as the build year and reports the wartime account as the Forest Service's.
The register's elevation field gives 8,134 ft (2,479 m). The Stanislaus note quoted in the register, and the trail guide, give 8,440 ft. The record's elevation_m (2479.2) follows the register field.

The Stanislaus note and the trail guide both give staffing as 1939-1973. The trail guide also says a small station stood near the peak until about the mid-1970s, a later date that no source read explains. The story reports the staffing span and the trail guide's station date separately, and does not say the sources differ on staffing.

notes_for_editor: Built, staffing and fate rest mainly on the register, which quotes a Stanislaus National Forest note; the 1934 construction is supported by two 1934 newspaper items as quoted on Forest Lookouts. The brief's note that another record shares register number US 1883, CA 78 was not resolved: the register page itself confirms that number for this site, and the other holder was not identified. The brief's 'ground' kind matches the register's 'ground cabin' wording. Access is recorded as public only because a hiking guide describes a trail to the site on national forest land; no closure or permit rule was read, so an editor may want a Stanislaus National Forest check before relying on the access level. The trail guide's account that the structure stood on the mountainside, and the glass-windowed station it recalls, were left out of the story because they come from a visitor's recollection on that page. Photos: the register lists a 1935 photo and a 2011 photo with credits, but no image URLs were captured, so none are listed.
